title: introduce-cost-orchestrator-slate-simulator-and-telemetry-bridge
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds Cost Orchestrator service which consumes aggregated telemetry, runs conservative unit-econ projections and a synthetic quant/batch simulator to propose tenant defaults. Exposed via API and redwoodctl. Feature-flagged behind econ_v2.
description: Summary: Adds a new internal service (cost-orchestrator) that ingests aggregated tenant telemetry, runs a deterministic econometric forecast, and executes a low-fidelity quant slate simulator to generate conservative recommendations for batching, cache settings, and quant tiers. Suggestions are surfaced through an API and a new 'redwoodctl cost suggest' command. Motivation: Many tenants keep overly conservative defaults or no defaults; operations and platform teams need a reproducible, safe way to propose improvements with an estimated savings and risk. Design: Telemetry bridge (Go) normalizes and windows metrics into tenant_savings_signals with 15m windows, rate-limited per-region. Forecasting stage (Python) projects baseline unit-econ and sensitivity to batch/cache/quant changes; tests include snapshot comparisons. Quant slate simulator (Python) uses runtime kernel profiles from the model-catalog to estimate latency, memory headroom, and token-cost for candidate quant tiers and batch shapes. Safety: Reject candidates exceeding a conservative latency multiplier (default 2.0) or with >5% simulated failure probability. Rollout: Feature-flagged (econ_v2); initial shadow run, small cohort enable, operator review before wider UI exposure. Changed files (high level): cmd/redwoodctl/cost_suggest.go, services/cost-orchestrator/main.go, services/cost-orchestrator/simulator/quant_slate.py, pkg/telemetry/bridge/consumer.go, infra/helm/cost-orchestrator/values.yaml, migrations/20260220_add_cost_orch_tables.sql, docs/operations/cost-orchestrator.md, sdk/python/redwood/savings.py. Testing: Unit tests for forecast model, integration harness against sample kernel profiles, staging perf canary in shadow mode. CI notes: fixed gofmt and flake8 issues; final CI: build/pass, unit tests/pass, integration tests/pass. Review highlights: Marco requested rate-limiting and cardinality docs (addressed), Leah asked about hardware-family fidelity (simulator uses kernel profiles and flags family-limited suggestions), Owen requested runbook and kill-switch (added). Migration and safety: additive DB migrations, restore-validated in staging, no changes to runtime serving path. Metrics & alerts added: savings_orch.generated_suggestions_total, savings_orch.simulator_latency_ms, savings_orch.proposal_confidence_histogram; alerts for high proposal error rate and slow simulator. Follow-ups: retrain pipeline cadence (ENG-8579), closed-loop validation for applied suggestions (PM-1377), higher-fidelity simulator for expanded hardware coverage. Merge: Squash-merged after approvals and green CI. Reviewer guidance: focus on consumer.go for rate/partition assumptions, quant_slate.py for safety thresholds, and migrations for restore safety.
